packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-04 - unverified image-only first reading

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of these fragments. The only labels seen are the modern pencil shelfmarks written on the fragments themselves ("Stams, STA, Frg. 260-1r ... 4v"). Beyond the stated rules: I listed the packet directory to get the image filenames, and I made enlarged crops of images 004, 005, 008, 009 and 010 with PIL in my own scratch directory to read faint ink. No other files were opened, and no web or search tools were used.

IMAGES
- image-001: overview of four small parchment slips laid out left to right, labelled (pencil) 260-4r, 260-3r, 260-2r and a fourth whose label is partly hidden (read as 260-1r). Colour chart and ruler: each slip is about 7.5-8 cm wide and 5.5-6 cm high.
- image-002: 260-4r. Blank, with a small hole and no visible writing.
- image-003: 260-3r.
- image-004: 260-2r.
- image-005: 260-1r (label partly illegible: "Stams, STA, Frg. 2[..]-1r"?).
- image-006: overview of the versos, labelled 260-4v, 260-3v, 260-2v, 260-1v.
- image-007: 260-4v. Blank.
- image-008: 260-3v.
- image-009: 260-2v.
- image-010: 260-1v.
The tiles each show one slip, with only slivers of the neighbouring slips at the edges. I did not count those slivers as additional text.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Each slip is a cut-down piece of a single column of text. No margin is preserved, except possibly on the left of 3r/3v. No running titles are visible. The script is a small gothic textualis book hand in brown ink, with red rubrics, red initials and red stroke-touching of capitals.
- 260-3r: a large red initial M with a long flourished tail running down to the lower left, spanning about 2 text lines. There is a red rubric in line 2. Below line 4 the slip is blank: either the text ends or the space was left unwritten (the M tail runs into that space).
- 260-2r: a red rubric line ("In .ii. nocturno" type) with a red two-line initial below it. There is a red paragraph sign / capital touching in line 4 and a red stroke at top.
- 260-1r: a red initial (looks like a squared "H", or an "E"/"R") at the top left, about 2 lines high. A faded/abraded red initial or ruling sits mid-slip.
- 260-1v and 260-2v: red-touched capitals and a red rubricated "A" with an overline (an abbreviation sign) on 1v.
- Interpretation (tentative): the red rubrics "Respon(sorium)", "In ii nocturno", "an(tiphona)" and "R" suggest a liturgical office book (breviary or lectionary-type text), with lessons in prose interspersed with responsory/antiphon cues. This is an interpretation of the visible rubrics only. I am not identifying the text.
- 260-3v: show-through (mirror-image) of the 3r text and of the red M is clearly visible. Only the first line is genuine verso text.

TRANSCRIPTION
Conventions: line numbers count from the top of each image; red = rubricated; (..) = expansion; ? = uncertain; [illegible] = unread. Abbreviation marks are described in brackets where I cannot render them.

--- image-003 (260-3r) ---
003.1  [top line cut through; only lower parts of letters] uncer? [illegible] ... [illegible]
003.2  [ink trace/flourish at left edge] mantei? / mantem? (letters "mante" + i or ? ) · (red:) T · Respon(sorium) [abbreviated "Respon" with superscript stroke]  (red, at right edge:) M[ (a red "m" with superscript, cut)
003.3  (red initial M, 2 lines) aria parens h[...]   [i.e. "M" + "aria parens h-", the h cut at the right edge]
003.4  [M continued] lios? · plangens [final letter cut; read "hios" / "lios" then "plangens"]
003.5ff  blank parchment below; only the red tail of the M. Pencil shelfmark.
Note on 003.2: the word before the red T reads "mantei" or "maneret"? Only the letters "-mante-" are secure. The red "T" is a single red capital, possibly a mark meaning "T(u autem)" or similar. I report the letter only.

--- image-004 (260-2r) ---
004.1  [cut at top] [.]n? pnimium? / primam? ... me (red:) V? [red mark] [illegible] n
       ["...m pn..." + "me" are partly visible; a red V-shaped sign follows; one letter "n" at right]
004.2  Felix sabbatum? / Felix [s]ab[.]ata? · du=   [Hyphen "=" at line end]. Read: "Felix sa[.]b[a]tia?" with a superscript/tilde over "ca"; uncertain.
004.3  [.]p[..]ta? / pirata? exultac(i)o? [abbreviated, tilde over "ac"] · da=
004.4  bant' [superscript 2-shaped mark = -ur?] in sep(?)h[i]e? · (red:) R [a red "R" with a stroke = responsorium?] (black, overwritten) m[ / an
       ["bant(ur)? in sepulcro?" is NOT secure. Visible letters: "bant²  in' seph?e · " then a red-touched "R/S" + "m"]
004.5  (red rubric:) In · ii.o (= secundo) nocturno · na[..]: [last word "nasc" or "nat" with abbreviation stroke; read "na[t]?" , cut at right]
004.6  (red 2-line initial, looks like N or H:) N[...] [illegible/faded] ... ue? xpc (= Christ-? "xp" with c? or "xpo"?)  [a hole sits above "ue"]
004.7  [initial continues] [faint, mostly abraded] ... [illegible]
004.8  [.]nt? / [ ]n[.]ry · n? gratis? / grat[.]s? ... [illegible] =
       [visible: "...m[..]ry · n' g'tis? ... ="]
004.9  [.]es? pueri? [/puer i] nascerib? / uilcerib(us)?  [line-end "-ib9" = -ibus]
       [I read "...ces pueri[.] ... rib(us)". The middle word looks like "nilcerib9", plausibly "uisceribus"?? (only "-ceribus" is fairly secure)]

--- image-005 (260-1r) ---
005.1  [top edge: red and black traces, cut; illegible]
005.2  (red initial, about 2 lines: H? / E?) [.]n mexanni? / in me[..]nim? a[ ]  [visible: "...m me[.]ania a/n" ; mostly uncertain]
005.3  [initial continues] [.]elium? / [.]estum? coe? · [illegible] illam? / illud?
005.4  [.]e' [illegible] ne? tme? / tunc? valde? / tradi? [superscript letter above "-de"]
005.5  [illegible] ... ta · [illegible] fuit? / suisse?
005.6  [abraded line with a faint red (initial or touched letter) at centre]: [illegible] ... ad hunc? / abrunt? [right part: "abrup"? / "ab inu[.]"]
005.7  [.]n monca? / montem? / in montem? [abbreviated] ducebat' (= ducebatur?) [line ends with ";" type punctus]
005.8  [.]que cirt? scem? / circumstantes?? : "que ciui[.]cem? sp(irit)u? [or "spe"] ..o =
       [Secure letters: "que ci?u?[s/f]cem? sp?c? nio?" plus line-end hyphen]
005.9  [bottom cut: only tops of letters]
This face is very faded. Of everything in this packet, the readings here are the least secure.

--- image-008 (260-3v) ---
008.1  matris digne · R  [red-touched R with a cross-stroke, likely the responsory sign; then a brown ink smear/flourish to the right edge]
008.2-3  Mirror-image show-through of 3r ("...parens..." / "...plangens..." and the red M). This is not verso text.
       There is one small red dot at the left of line 2, possibly genuine.
Rest blank.

--- image-009 (260-2v) ---
009.1  [cut at top: red flourish + traces] [illegible]
009.2  gaudebat? / gaudeat? · p(ri)ma? / p(ri)mu(m)? lu[ / lu=   [read "gaudebat : prima lu"; "gaudebat" with a superscript over "de" (b + abbreviation?)]
009.3  [.]ucrate? / cuitate? / [ci]uitate collaqui? / colloquior(um)? [final "-or" with 2-shaped r + abbreviation]
009.4  assp?iebat? / aspiciebat? [visible "assp[.]iebat"] · bona m[ / bonam? m=
009.5  [.]ue? [abbrev] in? (red-touched capital) Ierl[m] (= Ier(usa)l(e)m?, "Irlm" with a superscript stroke) in mon[te]? / in mo[n]=
009.6  [.]ns? / [.]ri? ce?ehmie? / celebratione? [obscured by a hole] aspic[ / apic=
       [visible: "...ns c[.]le[..]rme apic"; I cannot resolve the middle]
009.7  bat? · (red-touched capital, preceded by a red punctus) [S]oluit? / Volunt? ibi? / tibi? amic[ / nunc
       [visible: "bat · [red] Volue? ibi amic/nunc"]
009.8  [.]itti? / nitri? / uiri? ii? / u' [superscript s] in publico? ue[ / ne[
       [secure: "in publico"]
009.9  [bottom cut: tops of letters only]

--- image-010 (260-1v) ---
010.1  [.]nus? / -mus? [.]enit? / uenit? · (red:) an(tiphona) [followed by a red-touched letter and a flourish, cut]
010.2  sunt? / fuit? in cinere? / incineratae? · (red-touched capital) M[ ...] [cut at the right; "Ma[..]"]
010.3  [.]ultu(m)? / multu(m)? [?] a[.]sire? / auspice? · mon[.]a? / moui?[..]
       [visible "multu(m) a[.]pice · montel?/montid"]
010.4  frand[..]? / frande[.]? [hole] [.]b? · tempauit? / temperauit?  [visible "frand??? . tempauit"]
010.5  [.]e[.]rsum? / lacrimam? · ap(osto)l(u)s? / apt' (abbrev "apl" with superscript) morit[ / moru=
010.6  ostanc[...] / ostancti? / ostendit? · colloqui? / colloquio? sp(irit)?[ ...]  [visible "ostancti · colloqui[.] sp[...]" with a flourish]
010.7  ug[.]o? / ug[.]us? [?] · (red:) A· [red A with an overline = "A(ntiphona)"?] (red-touched capital) L[ ...] ongu? / Longe? / longue? ui[ / ui=
       [visible: "...gu[.]s · (red Ā·) L(red stroke) ongid? ui"]
010.8  ꝑtusit? / pertusit? / pertulit? · (red-touched capital) M[a]ri? / Martir? a? ... ma[  ["M..ri..ma" read loosely; "Maria"? not secure]
010.9  tes? / [.]e? circuit? / cirauit? · hilaris? ... [ / hilaris h[   ["... circuit · hilaris" fairly visible]
010.10 [bottom cut]

AREAS SELECTED AND UNREAD
- I attempted every inked line on every face. The faces were small enough that I did not need to select spans. Blank faces: 4r and 4v.
- The weakest areas are 1r (lines 2-8, very abraded), 2r lines 6-8 (abraded around the initial), and the right-edge cut words on all faces.
- No face shows ten or more lines: the slips hold at most 8-9 lines. Connected spans of that length are not physically available.

LIMITATIONS
- These are tiny cut-down slips (binding waste), cropped on all sides. Line ends and beginnings are lost or partial.
- 1r and 1v are heavily faded. Several words are given only as letter sequences, and some proposed words are guesses at the letter level.
- 3v carries strong show-through from 3r, which I excluded.
- I made no inference about the order of the slips relative to each other, and the slip numbers may not reflect original sequence. I could not determine column position or page layout.
- A higher-contrast or UV/multispectral image of 260-1r and 260-2r lines 6-8 would help most.
